2607.12634.title: Atomic Units of X: The Compression Layer of Intelligence
2607.12634.paper_summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for understanding intelligence as a process of atomic compression and compositional reuse. We argue that cognitive, biological, computational, and organizational systems achieve scalable intelligence by decomposing complex phenomena into reusable atomic units that can be recombined into higher-order structures. Drawing on evidence from cognitive science, information theory, evolutionary biology, software engineering, medicine, legal reasoning, education, music, and artificial intelligence, the paper develops the concept of atomic units as fundamental compression layers that support efficiency, transfer, interpretability, and evolvability. The central contribution is the Compression Calculus, a formal framework for comparing surface-level representations with atomic representations and for describing how compression gains compound across abstraction layers. We introduce the Compounding Cascade thesis, according to which each additional layer of abstraction multiplicatively increases representational efficiency rather than merely adding incremental savings. The paper further argues that contemporary AI systems often operate at suboptimal levels of representation, relying on token-level processing or document-level retrieval rather than stable, concept-level atomic structures. In this view, large language models are best understood not as complete knowledge architectures, but as dynamic fusion engines capable of navigating, sequencing, and recombining atomic units. The framework provides a foundation for designing self-evolving knowledge systems that can discover, refine, and compose new primitives over time. By reframing intelligence as compression through compositional abstraction, the paper offers a unifying perspective on expertise, knowledge representation, explainable AI, and the future architecture of adaptive intelligent systems.
2607.12634.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文提出了一個理論框架，以理解智慧作為一種原子壓縮和組合重用的過程。<lb/>我們認為，認知、生物、計算和組織系統通過將複雜現象分解為可重用的原子單位，並將其重新組合成更高階的結構，來實現可擴展的智慧。<lb/>論文借鑒了認知科學、信息理論、進化生物學、軟體工程、醫學、法律推理、教育、音樂和人工智慧的證據，發展了原子單位的概念，作為支持效率、轉移、可解釋性和可演化性的基本壓縮層。<lb/>中央貢獻是壓縮演算，一個正式的框架，用於比較表面層表示與原子表示，並描述壓縮增益如何在抽象層之間累積。<lb/>我們引入了複合級聯論，根據該論點，每增加一層抽象就會乘法性地提高表示效率，而不僅僅是增加增量節省。<lb/>論文進一步主張當代 AI 系統經常在次最佳的表示水平運行，依賴於標記級處理或文件級檢索，而不是穩定的概念級原子結構。<lb/>在這種觀點下，大型語言模型最好被理解為不是完整的知識架構，而是能夠導航、排序和重新組合原子單位的動態融合引擎。<lb/>該框架為設計自我演化的知識系統提供了基礎，這些系統可以隨著時間的推移發現、完善和組合新的原始元素。<lb/>通過將智慧重新框架為通過組合抽象進行的壓縮，這篇論文提供了一種統一的觀點，關於專業知識、知識表示、可解釋的 AI 以及適應性智能系統的未來架構。
